BERT4Rec trains on masked items and uses an appended mask for next-item inference ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690)). The weighting consequence follows algebraically: with mᵢ supervised targets in example i, pooled per-token loss is ΣᵢΣⱼℓᵢⱼ/Σᵢmᵢ; per-sequence loss is (1/B)Σᵢ(Σⱼℓᵢⱼ/mᵢ). Thus token averaging weights examples proportionally to target count, often favoring longer histories; sequence averaging gives each example equal total coefficient. For equal numbers of terminal examples and random-mask examples containing k targets each, token averaging assigns random-mask targets k/(k+1) of total loss weight—80% when k=4—whereas sequence averaging assigns each branch 50%. These are coefficients, not guaranteed gradient-norm shares: target difficulty and gradient alignment matter. PyTorch cross-entropy’s default mean averages nonignored targets, so flattening masked positions implements token averaging ([documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html)).

Recommended controlled ablations: first, reuse identical examples and masks while changing only reduction; explicit 0.5×terminal-mean + 0.5×random-sequence-mean guarantees equal branch coefficients. Second, compare terminal-only, exactly-one-random-mask, and their 50% mixture using matched users, sequence lengths, and one target per example; this removes supervision-count differences while testing target placement/context direction. Third, hold corrupted inputs fixed and compare supervising all masked positions versus one uniformly selected masked position, with sequence normalization; their expected gradients match, but gradient variance differs. Separately compare one-mask versus multiple-mask inputs while supervising one target to measure corruption effects. Cross masking conditions with identical full-history versus sampled-prefix length distributions. Keep architecture, initialization, optimizer, updates and evaluator fixed; report supervised-target counts, visible-context lengths and branch gradient norms. Target-budget-matched runs provide a separate supervision-volume control.
